description: Effective fleet configuration management in Go: declarative recipes, NATS-powered farmer/sprout agents, and fast parallel infrastructure automation

summary.one_liner: grlx is a pure-Go configuration management and DevOps automation engine that uses a central "farmer" server and "sprout" agents on managed nodes, driven by a CLI and YAML "recipes".
summary.what_it_does: grlx runs as three parts: a farmer daemon on a management server, sprout daemons on managed nodes, and a grlx command-line tool. The farmer embeds a NATS pub-sub bus and an API server, and sprouts subscribe to messages over that bus. Desired state is written as YAML documents called recipes, which are applied to sprouts with the "cook" command. The CLI can run locally on the farmer or remotely over a TLS-encrypted API. The README's quick start shows targeting all nodes to run connectivity tests and remote commands, with output available as JSON. The README says the farmer exposes an API so other tools could create jobs, but the CLI is the only supported method at this time.
use_cases: manage configuration across a fleet of Linux or macOS servers
push declarative desired-state recipes to many nodes
run ad hoc commands across all managed hosts
replace heavier Python-based config management tools
automate infrastructure setup with TLS-secured agents
how_to_run: Download the grlx CLI from releases and run: ./grlx init (choose farmer interface and ports, then note the admin public key)
On the control server, install the farmer using the bootstrap script from the README (curl ... | sudo bash)
On each node, install the sprout using the bootstrap script, setting FARMERINTERFACE to the farmer address
Run: grlx keys accept -A to accept sprout keys and TLS cert
notable: Pure-Go single-binary design aimed at low resource use, contrasted with Python-based tools
Embedded NATS message bus so sprouts subscribe to farmer messages without a separate broker
Public-key authentication for sprouts and TLS-encrypted API by default
Declarative YAML recipes applied with a cook command
Targeted ad hoc commands across fleet with -T glob-style selection
caveats: The README says the CLI is the only supported way to create jobs for now; the API is exposed but not officially supported for other clients
Quick start requires installing three components (CLI, farmer, sprouts) and manual key acceptance
Commercial and prioritized support is offered through a partner (ADAtomic, Inc.), and some package hosting depends on Cloudsmith
